content.text: I’ve got two concrete review items now. I’m pulling exact line numbers from the changed paths so the feedback is actionable rather than hand-wavy.

Findings:

1. Medium: [cmd/entire/cli/explain_summary_provider.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/explain_summary_provider.go:87) persists an auto-detected summary provider into whichever settings file `settingsTargetFile()` picks, and [cmd/entire/cli/setup.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:194) prefers `.entire/settings.json` when it exists. That means a read-only command path like `entire explain --generate` can silently dirty the branch with a machine-local PATH decision and commit a provider/model that may not exist for other developers. Since provider availability is explicitly host-local (`exec.LookPath`), this should either write to `settings.local.json` by default or avoid persistence unless the user explicitly configures it.

2. Medium: [cmd/entire/cli/setup.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:158) loads only the target file with `settings.LoadFromFile`, then [rejects `--summarize-model` unless that same file already has a provider](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:171). That breaks a valid override flow: if the project file defines `summary_generation.provider`, `entire configure --local --summarize-model ...` should be allowed, because merged runtime settings already support “provider from project, model from local”. The configure path currently ignores the inherited provider and errors out.

Assumptions / questions:

- I’m assuming summary-provider selection is intended to be machine-specific, because discovery is based on local CLI binaries rather than repo detection. If you explicitly want the provider choice to be shared repo-wide, finding 1 becomes less severe, but the command still has the surprising side effect of modifying tracked config during `explain`.

Change summary:

- I did not find an immediate correctness issue in the new Copilot VS Code compatibility or the condensation skip logic from the code/tests I checked.
- I also ran a focused Go test slice across the touched `agent`, `summarize`, `checkpoint`, `strategy`, `settings`, and `cli` packages; those targeted tests passed.
